quizName: Hardest Questions in Ohio Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots. What should riders do?

options.text: Check them regularly by turning your head.
They don't exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: How should you handle a driver who is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous by encouraging them to continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: What should an ideal lane position do?

options.text: Help you see others and be seen by them.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen by them.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It also keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a problem occurs.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding, no matter your speed. Wearing a proper, quality helmet greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position that makes you more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position that makes you more visible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that other drivers can see most clearly.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do first?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it immediately on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see your stop.
To look for dark clouds indicating bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see your stop.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see if drivers approaching from behind notice that you are stopping. Make sure they are responding appropriately to your actions.

questions.question: What makes good clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: It protects you in a crash.
It does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: Taking frequent rest breaks during long trips helps reduce fatigue. Caffeine and other stimulants can make fatigue worse when they wear off. Dress warmly and protect yourself from wind, rain, and snow on long trips.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long trip?
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you do not feel tired. Most experienced riders do not ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired quickly, so dress to protect yourself from the elements.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane of traffic.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.
More difficult than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark than in daylight. Shadows and light help you judge distance. At night, artificial lighting can distort or hide these important visual cues.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are weak.
May affect your riding and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can impair your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should you care about most?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your first priority when buying a helmet.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will remain in your body.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which material protects motorcycle riders best?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important factor. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and is DOT-compliant.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of a soft, pliable material.

questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Best increases your visibility and allows for a safe cushion of space.
You like, without regard to others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Best increases your visibility and allows for a safe cushion of space.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best and where you have room around your motorcycle. Good riders change their position as road conditions change.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the most protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection when riding.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards provides the best head and neck protection. Wearing a proper helmet is the single best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: Group riders should use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close while still maintaining safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: To make it easier to be seen by other motorists, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing while riding. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you, day or night.

questions.question: The proper action to take when riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time is to:

options.text: Just start riding. There is no better way to learn than by doing.
Just start riding. Most bikes are similar, so you don't have to take the time to identify safety features.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn the bike's gear pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, check its safety and maintenance. Find where everything is located. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how it operates.

questions.question: Whichever style of helmet you choose, you will get the most protection by ensuring that your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: Having only one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: Will not lead to a DUI conviction.
Will never affect your riding skills.
Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can impair your riding ability. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if you are below the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test each brake to make sure the brake lights work.
